transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Location: All-hands - Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel, Liam O'Connor, Priya Desai, Samir Kaur, Jordan Lee, Evan Brooks + company-wide

Summary:
Maya opens with company momentum and the need to codify an Ethical AI compact. Leadership updates on product launches (Dedicated rollout, Optimize recommendations), security/compliance progress, hiring posture, and Q4 priorities. Live Q&A about tradeoffs (latency vs cost, hosted vs private), and a short culture moment on incident postmortems and transparency.

Topics covered:
- Momentum + ARR and usage highlights
- Ethical AI compact — principles + enforcement
- Product updates: Dedicated, Private, Optimize
- Security & compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
- Hiring and org priorities
- Q&A and closing next steps

Action items: see metadata list above (leaders assigned)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I know it's a busy week, so we'll keep to about an hour, hour and change. Quick high level — we shipped two important things last month and usage is up across hosted and dedicated, which is, uh, great news.
[00:15] Applause / background noise
[00:22] Liam: Quick datapoint — 28% month over month increase in tokens served for mid-market accounts, and average 95th percentile latency is holding around 160ms on our smaller models under the new kernel scheduling. Some outliers on very long sequences but overall good.
[00:42] Noah (from Sales, misattributed as Speaker 3): couple of customers flagged a perf regression last week, turned out to be a config mismatch — Jordan already has a patch, and we're rolling to prod.
[00:55] Jordan: yeah, it was a runtime config where continuous-batching got set too high for a particular workload; we added a guard and a telemetry alert.
[01:10] Maya: Thank you. On the bigger topic, we need a company-level statement about responsible product behavior — we're calling it an "Ethical AI compact" for now. Not a long policy doc, but a short public-facing set of commitments plus internal guardrails. Priya?
[01:26] Priya: The compact should cover three things: safety/quality thresholds (how we measure regressions), data handling promises (no long-term customer content retention unless agreed), and operational fallback policies — for example if a model fails QA we route to degraded-but-safe variants. Also we should be clear about who signs off on escalations.
[01:45] Samir: For safety thresholds we can tie to our existing evals — prompt sets, adversarial tests, and monitoring. We'll publish a metrics baseline and example failure modes. Note: transcription here might say "adversarial tests" as somethin else sometime, sorry.
[02:02] Rina (Security): From compliance perspective, compact should reference SOC2 controls, KMS integration for private deployments, and transparent audit logs. Customers ask for 'bring your own key' (BYOK) often; we need a consistent messaging.
[02:18] Maya: Good. The compact will live on the public website and we'll also have an internal version with rollout checklists. Plan: draft by end of next week, internal review, then public short-form doc.
[02:30] [15 second pause / keyboard clatter]
[02:45] Evan: Quick on finances — we remain on plan but Q4 will be tight if we don't improve unit economics on hosted. The Optimize tooling suggestions have reduced per-token cost in pilots by ~12% but not universally. Need product + engineering to prioritize the highest-impact recommendations.
[03:05] Priya: We're scheduling a partner demo for Redwood Optimize next month to show batching/caching gains and recommended quantization profiles; that's on 2026-11-10.
[03:18] Maya: On product rollouts — Dedicated is in limited GA to two customers, and we have the Dedicated autoscaling work queued. Jordan?
[03:29] Jordan: Limited GA went okay. We learned a lot around cold-starts and KV cache warm-up for multi-tenant transitions; we've added smart warm-up policies and a fallback to smaller pinned model variants to avoid long tail latency. We'll publish a technical note.
[03:50] Liam: Also kernel selection improvements helped with memory overhead — some transcriptions might show "K V cash" or "K V cache" weirdly in meeting notes but it's KV cache.
[04:05] Samir: Small research update — our on-device quantization experiments show promising cost savings for embeddings without major quality loss; still need more evals on long form generation.
[04:20] Ava (Developer): quick question — how do we expect teams to flag quality regressions to engineering?
[04:28] Jordan: Use the product issues channel and tag the on-call SE; we'll triage with an established severity matrix. we'll add a template to reduce back-and-forth.
[04:40] Maya: People ops/hiring — we are prioritizing infra SRE, two senior infra engineers, and one security engineer for Q1. We're not doing a broad hiring freeze but being careful around headcount.
[04:55] Evan: Financially we modeled three scenarios; the board favors the middle path with modest hiring and increased focus on mid-market expansion.
[05:10] [Audience murmur — "ok", "good"]
[05:20] Open Q/A:
[05:22] Employee (text question read by host): is the Ethical AI compact going to affect our go-to-market messaging?
[05:27] Priya: It will — we'll add a short FAQ for sales and partner teams and a one-pager summarizing key customer promises.
[05:35] Employee (voice): Any change to data retention defaults for hosted accounts?
[05:40] Rina: No immediate default changes; we'll propose a clearer default and opt-in options for longer retention. For customers needing residency we already support region pinning and Private options.
[05:50] Employee: Will the compact include enforcement (penalties for misuse)?
[05:54] Maya: We'll define a set of remediation steps and, for public customers, reserve the right to suspend access for clear policy violations. Legal will help word this.
[06:05] Employee (Sam): Are we open sourcing any parts of our runtime work?
[06:10] Liam: We will open source some non-sensitive tooling and lightweight libraries, but not the kernel optimizations or specific heuristics that are operational secrets.
[06:18] [small chuckle / agreement]
[06:25] Closing remarks:
[06:27] Maya: Two asks — read the compact draft when it lands, and if you care deeply about the wording, take the review slot. Second, support the product teams in the next two weeks as we stabilize Dedicated GA and finalize Optimize partner materials. We'll have a follow-up town hall focusing exclusively on the compact if needed. Thanks everyone.
[06:45] End of meeting, applause, informal breakout rooms open

Notes about transcription quality: occasional mis-attributed speakers, filler words and short crosstalk, proper nouns occasionally garbled (e.g., KV cache -> K V cash). The transcript intentionally preserves natural speech and mild transcription artifacts.
